surfaces.part: lower crate slatted front with weak ledge

answer.evidence: In the brown crate (x=8), rows 1-4 are a plank lid band with a light tan front-edge line at row 5. Row 6 is a darker shadow row, and the slatted front runs from row 7 to the base at rows 14-15 (about 9 rows). The green crate on the right follows the same structure. The lid band is about 5 rows including the edge line, which is more than a 1-2 row rim. The lower crate shows only a faint ledge at rows 9-10, but it is mostly hidden by the stacked crate, so I count it as occluded. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small prop, roughly two tiles wide. Its measured facts are fine: 9 visible tones per tile (the same as the hedge, below the stall at 17 and the well at 20), 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels. So the outlines are tinted dark material tones rather than a black sticker line, and there are no flat fills. At 15 distinct colours across two crate materials, each ramp has only about 3-4 steps (highlight, mid, dark, outline), against the 5-6 steps of the stall and well. Texture is limited to a few plank lines and slat marks, with no per-plank grain, nail dots or wear speckle, so the 'weathered' quality is thin. The crates also read as two boxes side by side, not a stack with one on top. The slatted fronts and plank lids are only lightly articulated. Placed next to the stall and well references it looks flatter and thinner, so it does not clear the bar.

Below that, rows 6-15 are a slatted front with dark slat gaps at rows 6 and 9 and a dark base at rows 14-15. Both crates therefore show a top of about 5 rows above a front face of 9 or more rows, which is a three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small two-crate prop: one brown wood crate and one teal crate, with plank lids and slats. It measures 9 visible tones per tile, equal to prop-hedge and below the stall (17) and well (20), which are much larger and more detailed pieces. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills; slat lines, lid planks and per-plank value shifts break up each surface. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean toward the crate's own dark brown or dark teal rather than black, matching Beodeul's material-tone edges. Each material ramp has about 4 steps against roughly 5 in the references, which is a little shallower. Texture is present but modest, with little grain or speckle. As a simple crate prop it holds up next to the hedge and bench at the same scale, and a careful artist would accept it without it looking sticker-like.
